title: `can o.op(args)` — a permission query answers whether the operation's own gates would let it run on the bound row
note: A `requires` that reads the argument and the row and a `when` that reads the row, asked through a routed queryHandler before and after the operation runs, on every backend.

authzGate.//: `ship(c)`'s `requires c != code` reads the argument and the row, not the caller: the fixture's `test e2e` drives its 403 and its 204. The derived `can_ship` probe cannot decide a gate that reads a parameter, so it answers `{ allowed: false }`, a 200 (the gate order, docs/auth.md); the routed permission query decides it.
